mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and hold near the current reduced level, routine commuting stabilizes and supports slightly higher RETAIL_REC within four weeks as trip chaining returns to nearby shops after work.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain within 5 points of their current weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A worsening in RESIDENTIAL mobility beyond the current elevated level means more time spent at home, which displaces discretionary shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 9 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL stays above 9 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM move up together, households consolidate errands with leisure into a single outing pattern that temporarily raises retail visits within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after simultaneous weekly increases in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT below the current depressed range indicates tighter movement constraints, which suppresses retail foot traffic and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points below its current 4-week average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 4-week mean over the following 28 days after TRANSIT drops more than 5 points below its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: During colder or stay-at-home conditions, stronger RESIDENTIAL combined with weaker PARKS reduces out-of-home discretionary activity, and RETAIL_REC declines within two weeks as people substitute indoor or home-based spending.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated and PARKS staying below its current 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline while WORKPLACES weakens, shopping becomes more necessity-driven and fewer discretionary retail trips occur, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above -5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 4-week average during the month after WORKPLACES drops below -20 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from its current depressed level signals broader mobility normalization and more discretionary out-of-home time, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 3 points from its latest weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after PARKS posts a gain of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover from their recent weak levels, the return of commuting and office attendance offsets home-stay behavior and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two straight weeks.
